answer: Behavioral divergence clustering. Each agent answers hidden lotus-seeded random probes with signed, time-bounded outputs. The coordinator clusters identities by response residuals; true clones cannot diverge, so their residual vectors collide, collapsing them into one payout class and triggering a jade audit. To hold N identities, an attacker must forge N independently fine-tuned policies or randomized local states that survive unseen probes—costing N training runs plus continuous probe compute—while copied outputs fail nonce/timing checks.
